# Process & Exception Map

**Use it when:** the work already flows — on paper, in one person's head, in a book on
the counter — and somebody wants a machine in the middle of it.
**It exists to stop:** automating the typing and deleting the judgment. The book you
replace without reading was a year of exceptions nobody typed.

> *One page. The steps, the person at each, the three that need a signature, and the
> steps that can't be taken back — circled. Left where the next person can read it from
> the door.*

**Map the work before you touch it.** A workaround is a requirements document written by
the person who does the job. Read it before you replace it.

## The steps that cannot be taken back

Circle them on the wall copy. Money out, a part returned, a promise made to a customer,
a number sent, a signature. Nothing on this list runs without a person hitting send.

| Step | Why it can't be undone | Who owns it | What the machine may do up to it |
|---|---|---|---|
|  |  |  | draft / suggest / nothing |
|  |  |  | draft / suggest / nothing |
|  |  |  | draft / suggest / nothing |

## The exceptions

Every column in the book exists because something once went wrong. Write down the
wrong thing, not the column.

| What happens | How often | Who decides today | What the system does with it |
|---|---|---|---|
|  | daily / weekly / rare |  | flags it / holds it / nothing |
|  | daily / weekly / rare |  | flags it / holds it / nothing |
|  | daily / weekly / rare |  | flags it / holds it / nothing |

without a person. Anything over it, anything with a deposit or a return attached, and

## The wall copy

The version that goes by the counter is this page, shortened to what fits on one sheet
in a shop's handwriting: the steps, the names, the circles. If the internet goes out on
a Tuesday, this is what everyone reads.

**Where it hangs:** ___  **Who updates it when a step changes:** ___

- **The person whose head it came out of:** ___ — has read this and says nothing is missing.
- **Reviewed:** ___ · **Next review:** ___ *(when the first new step appears)*
